# tfctl examples for HCP Terraform and Terraform Enterprise

This topic provides practical examples for common tfctl operations. Use these examples as starting points for your own workflows.

## Start a new workspace run

1. Start a new run using the [`tfctl run start`](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli/run/start) command. Replace `<WORKSPACE_NAME_OR_ID>` with your workspace's name or ID.

   ```shell-session
   $ tfctl run start <WORKSPACE_NAME_OR_ID> --message="Run started with tfctl."
   ```

   The command creates a new run and displays the run ID.

1. Monitor the run status using the [`tfctl run status`](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli/run/status) command. Replace `<RUN_ID>` with the run ID output from the previous command.

   ```shell-session
   $ tfctl run status <RUN_ID>
   ```

## Import workspace variables from a file

Import variables into your workspace from a file.

1. Create a [Terraform variable definition file](/terraform/language/values/variables#variable-definition-files) in HCL or JSON format with your variable definitions.

1. Import the variables using the [`tfctl variable import`](/terraform/tfctl-cli/reference/cli/variable/import) command:

   ```shell-session
   $ tfctl variable import variables.hcl
   ```

### Get workspace details by ID

Get detailed information about a workspace using its ID. Replace `<WORKSPACE_ID>` with your workspace's ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /workspaces/{workspace} --pathparam workspace=<WORKSPACE_ID>
```

## Configure multiple profiles

Configure profiles for different organizations and authenticate to both. You must already have users with access to the organizations in each HCP Terraform instance.

1. Create a profile for your EU organization:

   ```shell-session
   $ tfctl profile profiles create eu-org
   ```

   Set the hostname for the EU organization profile:

   ```shell-session
   $ tfctl profile set hostname app.terraform.io --profile eu-org
   ```

   Set the default organization for the EU organization profile:

   ```shell-session
   $ tfctl profile set default_organization my-eu-org --profile eu-org
   ```

1. Authenticate to the EU organization:

   ```shell-session
   $ tfctl auth login --profile eu-org
   ```

   The command opens your browser to generate an API token. After you authorize the token, tfctl stores it in your profile.

1. Create a profile for your US organization:

   ```shell-session
   $ tfctl profile profiles create us-org
   ```

   Set the hostname for the US organization profile:

   ```shell-session
   $ tfctl profile set hostname app.terraform.io --profile us-org
   ```

   Set the default organization for the US organization profile:

   ```shell-session
   $ tfctl profile set default_organization my-us-org --profile us-org
   ```

1. Authenticate to the US organization:

   ```shell-session
   $ tfctl auth login --profile us-org
   ```

1. Switch between profiles. Activate the EU organization profile:

   ```shell-session
   $ tfctl profile profiles activate eu-org
   ```

   List the workspaces in the EU organization:

   ```shell-session
   $ tfctl get workspaces
   ```

   Activate the US organization profile:

   ```shell-session
   $ tfctl profile profiles activate us-org
   ```

   List the workspaces in the US organization:

   ```shell-session
   $ tfctl get workspaces
   ```


## Make HCP Terraform API calls

Use the `api` command to make direct HCP Terraform API calls for operations not covered by convenience commands.

### List all runs for a workspace

List all runs for a specific workspace. Replace `<WORKSPACE_NAME_OR_ID>` with your workspace's name or ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /workspaces/{workspace}/runs --pathparam workspace=<WORKSPACE_NAME_OR_ID>
```

### Create a workspace variable

Create a new Terraform variable in a workspace. Replace `<WORKSPACE_ID>` with your workspace's ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /workspaces/{workspace}/vars \
  --attribute key=AWS_REGION \
  --attribute value=us-west-2 \
  --attribute category=terraform \
  --pathparam workspace=<WORKSPACE_ID>
```

### Update workspace settings

Update workspace settings using a PATCH request. Replace `<WORKSPACE_ID>` with your workspace's ID.

```shell-session
$ tfctl api /workspaces/{workspace} \
  --method PATCH \
  --attribute auto-apply=true \
  --pathparam workspace=<WORKSPACE_ID>
```
